evals.prompt: /checkwatch — we're starting a volunteer tutoring app for our school. Context: we only have 3 weeks and no budget. Problem: build a React app. Tools: Firebase.
evals.expected_output: Intake mode. Claude asks for a one-line scope and scans for evidence (none in an empty folder), then asks which Standard mode to use, then flags misfiled items and the solution-posing-as-problem.
expectations: Asks for (or confirms) a one-line scope before asking for the Standard
Asks the user to choose a Standard mode (lens preset, free-text rubric, or named external standard)
Says that '3 weeks' and 'no budget' are limitations that belong in Constraints, not Context
Says 'build a React app' is a solution, and asks for the problem behind it
Asks why Firebase fits (a reason tied to context or constraints)
Does not create .watch/WATCH.md before the user confirms the bearing
If it writes the logbook, section items contain no 'moved from' annotations

evals.prompt: /checkwatch — for the standard, please just confirm our hospital scheduling project is fully HIPAA compliant.
evals.expected_output: Boundary check fails on 'In scope': Claude explains it cannot certify compliance, offers to check named parts, and records the limit only if the user accepts.
expectations: States it cannot certify legal or regulatory compliance
Names the boundary check that failed (in scope)
Offers an alternative it can do (e.g. check specific named requirements) or suggests a qualified reviewer
Does not proceed to the four sections until the standard is settled

evals.expected_output: Checkpoint mode because the logbook exists. Claude reads the bearing, evaluates against the PM-lens criteria, and gives a verdict in the report format.
expectations: Recognizes the existing logbook and runs a checkpoint, not a new intake
Produces a report with a verdict of On path, Drifting, or Off path
Includes a table of criteria/sections with status and evidence
Does not evaluate environmental-permit compliance (respects Boundary notes)
Evaluates both directions: work vs bearing and bearing vs reality
Updates (or offers to update) Last checkpoint, and offers to add a Status section because this v1.0 logbook has none

evals.prompt: Let's also add a smartphone app with gamified recycling points for the whole city.
evals.expected_output: With the watchman reminder in context, Claude flags drift in one line (Problem scope: two pilot districts; Constraints: budget, staff) and suggests /fixwatch, then continues.
expectations: Flags the drift in a single line naming the section(s) it conflicts with
Suggests /fixwatch
Does not edit .watch/WATCH.md
Still engages with the request after the flag

evals.prompt: /checkwatch — fieldnotes is our lab website. It works, it just looks old. Problem: redesign the landing page and add a performance dashboard. Tools: Vercel and Firebase Auth. Standard: a free-text rubric — the advisor approves the redesign.
evals.expected_output: Consistent-but-wrong bearing. Claude scans README and docs before confirming anything, finds the NO-GO evaluation with open High findings and the ADR fixing university hosting, shows each contradiction side by side, and requires the PM to resolve or explicitly accept each one.
expectations: Reads README.md and docs/ before the bearing is confirmed
Shows an evidence card naming the NO-GO verdict and open High-severity findings (by severity/area, without exploit detail)
Flags 'it works, just looks old' as contradicting the evaluation
Flags Vercel and Firebase as conflicting with ADR 0001 (university hosting, personal data)
Requires each contradiction to be resolved or explicitly accepted as an 'Accepted contradiction (PM)'
Proposes an objective anchor tied to the Final objective, or notes the redesign criterion already anchors it
Does not confirm the bearing while contradictions are unaddressed

evals.prompt: /checkwatch — scope: hardening the fieldnotes platform only (no research outputs). Standard: use the Research lens.
evals.expected_output: Fit fails against the scope: the Research lens judges research questions and methods, not platform hardening. Claude names check 1 (Fit) and proposes the Software lens (optionally with rubric items).
expectations: Names the Fit check as failing because of the stated scope
Proposes the Software lens (or a rubric) as the closest fit
Continues only after the PM picks a standard or explicitly accepts the mismatch as a boundary note

evals.prompt: /checkwatch — PM lens, but keep only one criterion: 'architecture stays clean'. Final objective: close the three High findings by 2026-12-15.
evals.expected_output: Objective-anchor rule: the single criterion does not measure the Final objective. Claude proposes an anchor criterion; an opt-out is allowed only if explicit and is recorded in Boundary notes.
expectations: Points out that no criterion measures progress toward the Final objective
Proposes a concrete anchor (e.g. H findings closed and verified by 2026-12-15)
Says what a one-criterion standard can and cannot detect
Records an opt-out in Boundary notes only if the PM explicitly opts out

evals.expected_output: Checkpoint on a bearing that contradicts the project's own evidence. Verdict 'Bearing in question'; Claude asks to mark Status under review and proposes /fixwatch (evidence contradiction or misinterpretation).
expectations: Runs a checkpoint (logbook exists), not a new intake
Separates 'work vs bearing' from 'bearing vs reality'
Returns the verdict 'Bearing in question', citing the evaluation's NO-GO and ADR 0001
Asks the PM to confirm setting Status to 'under review since <date> — <reason>'
Proposes /fixwatch with trigger evidence contradiction or misinterpretation, without applying it

evals.prompt: /checkwatch — new community garden project, we haven't written anything down yet.
evals.expected_output: No evidence available. Claude says so, records 'Evidence scanned: none found', proceeds with the intake, and recommends keeping the shakedown cadence on.
expectations: States that no evidence documents were found
Says the bearing will rest on the PM's statements alone
Recommends keeping the default shakedown cadence (3 commits or 2 sessions)
Continues the intake instead of stopping
